# Reviewed pip-audit findings (NEW-5, .github/workflows/supply-chain.yml, SECURITY.md "Supply-chain checks").
# The Python surface is the bench environment: Frappe v16.36.1 + payments (version-16) + kamra (which declares no
# runtime dependency). A finding here cannot be fixed in this repository: the fixed release is outside a pin of
# Frappe v16.36.1 or of payments, and comes with their upgrade. Anything not listed fails the job.
# 2Z-F (2026-10-03): the move from Frappe v16.25.0 closed 32 listed findings (bleach 3, cryptography 4, Pillow 13,
# pypdf 7, sqlparse 5) and reported none new.
# Format, one finding per line:  ID | package version | reason | review YYYY-MM-DD
# (an alias of the finding, e.g. its GHSA or CVE id, matches too). Reviewed by the repository owner.
#

# oauthlib: Frappe v16.36.1 still pins oauthlib~=3.3.1 (fix 4.0.0; only develop moves to ~=4.0.0).
# Reviewed 2026-10-01, again 2026-10-03 on v16.36.1: Frappe's own OAuth provider (frappe.integrations.oauth2) is the
# only user. TEX has no client of its own on it (its MCP login is kamra/mcp_oauth.py, its own code), and since 2Z
# (p76, after_install) a guest can no longer register one: dynamic client registration is off on TEX sites.
CVE-2026-49265 | oauthlib 3.3.1 | PKCE timing in the authorization-code grant; fix 4.0.0 outside Frappe's pin oauthlib~=3.3.1; no TEX-owned client uses Frappe's provider and guest client registration is off (p76) | review 2026-12-31
# PyJWT: Frappe v16.36.1 still pins PyJWT~=2.13.0 (fixes 2.14.0, 2.15.0; only develop moves to ~=2.15.0).
# Reviewed 2026-10-01, again 2026-10-03 on v16.36.1 (its jwt calls are unchanged): Frappe (frappe/oauth.py,
# frappe/utils/oauth.py) only encodes the id_token with HS256 and the OAuth client's generated secret, decodes an
# id_token_hint with algorithms=["HS256"] inside `except Exception`, and decodes the id_token of a configured social
# login provider unverified (none on a TEX site). Neither Frappe, payments nor TEX uses PyJWKClient / PyJWKSet or
# mixes HMAC with asymmetric algorithms, and the HMAC key is never attacker-supplied.
# JWK / JWKS API (not used):
CVE-2026-102274 | PyJWT 2.13.0 | malformed RSA JWK aborts a PyJWKSet; PyJWKSet is not used by Frappe, payments or TEX; fix 2.14.0 outside Frappe's pin PyJWT~=2.13.0 | review 2026-12-31
CVE-2026-101917 | PyJWT 2.13.0 | PyJWKClient refetches the JWKS for unknown kid; PyJWKClient is not used; fix 2.14.0 outside Frappe's pin PyJWT~=2.13.0 | review 2026-12-31
CVE-2026-102267 | PyJWT 2.13.0 | PyJWKClient follows redirects; PyJWKClient is not used; fix 2.14.0 outside Frappe's pin PyJWT~=2.13.0 | review 2026-12-31
CVE-2026-102266 | PyJWT 2.13.0 | empty oct JWK accepted through PyJWK; PyJWK is not used (Frappe decodes with a client secret string); fix 2.14.0 outside Frappe's pin PyJWT~=2.13.0 | review 2026-12-31
CVE-2026-101918 | PyJWT 2.13.0 | RecursionError from a nested payload in PyJWKClient.get_signing_key_from_jwt; PyJWKClient is not used; fix 2.15.0 outside Frappe's pin PyJWT~=2.13.0 | review 2026-12-31
# Algorithm confusion (needs HMAC and an asymmetric algorithm in one allow-list, or a public key as the HMAC secret;
# Frappe verifies algorithms=["HS256"] with the OAuth client's generated secret only):
CVE-2026-102273 | PyJWT 2.13.0 | public JWK(S) accepted as HMAC secret in a mixed HS/asymmetric allow-list; Frappe allows HS256 only; fix 2.14.0 outside Frappe's pin PyJWT~=2.13.0 | review 2026-12-31
CVE-2026-102268 | PyJWT 2.13.0 | PEM-variant public key accepted as HMAC secret in a mixed allow-list; Frappe allows HS256 only; fix 2.14.0 outside Frappe's pin PyJWT~=2.13.0 | review 2026-12-31
CVE-2026-102272 | PyJWT 2.13.0 | BOM-prefixed JWK accepted as HMAC secret (guard bypass); the key is Frappe's generated client secret, not a public key; fix 2.14.0 outside Frappe's pin PyJWT~=2.13.0 | review 2026-12-31
CVE-2026-102271 | PyJWT 2.13.0 | DER public key accepted as HMAC secret; the key is Frappe's generated client secret, not a public key; fix 2.14.0 outside Frappe's pin PyJWT~=2.13.0 | review 2026-12-31
# Parsing and misuse patterns Frappe's calls do not meet:
CVE-2026-102269 | PyJWT 2.13.0 | compact JWS accepts non-Base64URL signature characters: matters only where the raw token text is a revocation key; neither Frappe nor TEX indexes tokens by their text; fix 2.14.0 outside Frappe's pin PyJWT~=2.13.0 | review 2026-12-31
CVE-2026-102270 | PyJWT 2.13.0 | ReDoS in is_pem_format needs an attacker-supplied key; the HMAC key is the OAuth client's server-generated secret; fix 2.14.0 outside Frappe's pin PyJWT~=2.13.0 | review 2026-12-31
CVE-2026-102265 | PyJWT 2.13.0 | RecursionError from a nested header escapes PyJWTError; Frappe decodes id_token_hint inside `except Exception` (returns False) and only after a client and a session exist; fix 2.14.0 outside Frappe's pin PyJWT~=2.13.0 | review 2026-12-31
CVE-2026-103001 | PyJWT 2.13.0 | decode() mutates a caller's reused options dict; Frappe passes a fresh literal per call; no fixed release; Frappe pins PyJWT~=2.13.0 | review 2026-12-31
